deep.reconstruction: The page has no mathematics. It is a wrapper or title sheet. Near the left-centre is a single ink heading, 'Nobilische Farbenringe' (Nobili's colour rings), and it appears struck through. The archival folio number (200) is circled at the right. On the right margin there are a few very faint pencil marks (something like '+ 5004 = 1…' and possibly '84'), which cannot be read reliably. They may be an unrelated calculation or show-through. No derivation, formula or argument can be reconstructed. The heading is clearly a label for a bundle of notes on Nobili's rings. These are the coloured interference rings formed when a metal oxide or peroxide film (e.g. lead peroxide) is deposited electrolytically on a metal plate under a point electrode. Riemann published on this topic in 'Über die Theorie der Nobili'schen Farbenringe' (Poggendorff's Annalen der Physik 95, 1855). There he treated the current distribution in the electrolyte and plate as a potential problem and derived the thickness distribution of the deposited layer. The strike-through most likely marks the wrapper as processed or reused. The facing page (habilitation-related notes on trigonometric series and Dirichlet/Fourier) is unrelated in content, so this sheet is a separate folder cover.
